events.title: US–Iran war: ceasefire talks stall, Trump rejects Iran's 7-day proposal
events.why_it_matters: Seven months of war with Iran has kept Brent above $100 and Strait of Hormuz flows disrupted; Trump's rejection of Tehran's ceasefire plan keeps the oil-risk premium and inflation impulse alive.
events.what_to_watch: Whether mediators (Qatar/Oman) revive an amended 7-day ceasefire and whether Hormuz fuel-shipment flows normalize.

events.title: Brent crude tops $100 then slips below $98 on Iran-talk swings
events.why_it_matters: Oil above $100 is a direct tax on consumers and a key input to the Fed's inflation problem, driving the October hike odds.
events.what_to_watch: Daily Brent direction around ceasefire headlines and whether fuel-product shortages persist even as crude flows recover.

events.title: September jobs report (NFP) — consensus ~84k, U3 ~4.1%
events.why_it_matters: First payrolls print after the Sept 16 hike; ADP came in hot at +90k, so a strong NFP would cement October hike odds while a miss would reprice them sharply lower.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs ~84k consensus, prior-month revisions, and average hourly earnings for the wage-inflation signal.

events.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting — output policy decision
events.why_it_matters: With Brent above $100 on Iran-war supply risk, OPEC+ must decide whether to keep the 2 mb/d cut in place or signal unwinding; a surprise output increase would hit crude and energy equities.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the group holds the cut through end-2026 or hints at tapering given elevated prices.

events.title: FOMC minutes of the September 15–16 hike meeting
events.why_it_matters: Minutes will reveal how close the Committee was to 50 bp vs 25 bp and the bar for another hike at the Oct 27–28 meeting, where markets price ~73% odds of a hike.
events.what_to_watch: Language on inflation persistence, oil pass-through, and any dissent on the size of the move.

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: First major consumer-staples print of Q3 season; will show whether tariff-driven input costs and soft volumes are pressuring pricing power.
events.what_to_watch: Organic revenue growth, North America beverage volumes, and any FY guidance revision.

events.title: Q3 2026 bank earnings kickoff — JPM, BAC, WFC, Citi, GS
events.why_it_matters: Big-bank results open Q3 earnings season and set the tone for credit conditions, net interest income under a hiking Fed, and capital-markets activity.
events.what_to_watch: NII guidance, loan-loss provisions, trading revenue, and any commentary on consumer credit stress.

events.title: UnitedHealth Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: UNH is the healthcare bellwether and a Dow component; its medical-cost trend and guidance drive the managed-care complex and the sector's 2027 outlook.
events.what_to_watch: Medical loss ratio, Medicare Advantage cost trends, and any 2027 guidance framework.

events.title: ASML Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: ASML is the lithography chokepoint for AI-chip capacity; bookings and China revenue mix are a leading indicator for the whole semi-equipment complex.
events.what_to_watch: Net bookings, 2027 guidance, and China sales exposure under export controls.

events.title: September CPI — consensus ~3.7% headline
events.why_it_matters: The single most important print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC; with oil above $100 and CPI near 3.4–3.7%, a hot number locks in an October hike and pressures equities.
events.what_to_watch: Core CPI month-over-month, shelter and energy components, and whether the print shifts the ~73% October hike odds.

events.title: September retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Consumer confidence is near a 12.5-year low amid labor-market fears; retail sales will show whether the consumer is holding up under higher rates and $100 oil.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales and whether gasoline-price-driven spending masks underlying weakness.

events.title: China Q3 GDP and September activity data
events.why_it_matters: Q3 GDP tests whether China's mini-stimulus (PSL cut, mortgage subsidies) is enough to hold the 4.5–5% target after H1 growth of 4.7% and a soft Q2 at 4.3%.
events.what_to_watch: Q3 GDP print, September industrial production, retail sales, and property investment.

events.title: China September trade data (exports/imports)
events.why_it_matters: Exports have been China's growth engine (Aug exports +25% y/y); the print shows whether front-running of tariff changes is inflating shipments ahead of the truce expiry.
events.what_to_watch: Export growth vs prior +25%, and any shift in shipments to the US after the $60bn tariff-relief list.

events.title: China stimulus follow-through: PSL cut, mortgage subsidies, relending quotas
events.why_it_matters: PBOC cut the 1-year PSL rate 25 bp to 1.5% and raised relending quotas for tech and small business, plus first-time-buyer mortgage subsidies — but markets judged it a 'mini-stimulus' that secures the target without a broad revival.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the PBOC follows with an LPR cut or RRR reduction, and whether property sales respond.

events.title: US–China trade truce extended; $60bn tariff-relief list published
events.why_it_matters: Trump–Xi summit extended the truce to Jan 10, 2027 and both sides listed $60bn of goods for reciprocal tariff cuts, cutting near-term tariff-cliff risk though soybeans, semis and EVs remain unresolved.
events.what_to_watch: Formal implementation of the tariff-cut list, the new Board of Trade, and whether the BIS affiliates-rule suspension holds.

events.title: Boeing SPEEA engineers contract vote — strike risk after Oct 6
events.why_it_matters: A second rejection of Boeing's improved offer (4% guaranteed raises) could trigger a strike by 17,000 engineers and technical workers, disrupting aircraft development and production.
events.what_to_watch: Thursday vote outcome and whether SPEEA sets a strike date after Oct 6.

events.title: Micron FY2026 Q4 record results — AI memory supercycle confirmed
events.why_it_matters: Micron reported record Q4/FY26 revenue of $133.19bn (vs $37.38bn prior year) with EPS ~$31.50, validating HBM/DRAM pricing strength and lifting the whole memory and AI-semi complex.
events.what_to_watch: Forward HBM pricing commentary and whether the record results sustain the AI-capex trade into Q4.

events.title: Nike Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global consumer bellwether reporting after the close, with shares at 12-year lows; results signal demand, China trends, and inventory health for the apparel cycle.
events.what_to_watch: China revenue, gross margin, and FY guidance against the ~$11.3bn sales bar.

events.title: FOMC September hike to 3.75–4.00% — first hike since 2023
events.why_it_matters: The regime-changing event of the window: a unanimous 25 bp hike reset the discount-rate path for equities, credit, housing and the dollar, and markets now price ~73% odds of another hike Oct 27–28.
events.what_to_watch: Whether CPI/NFP keep the October hike on track and how much further the terminal rate extends.

events.title: Fed officials signal October hike on the table (Barr, Williams)
events.why_it_matters: Fed speakers reinforced that another hike is possible at the October meeting, keeping rate-sensitive assets under pressure.
events.what_to_watch: Further Fed commentary and whether officials push back on or validate the ~73% October hike odds.

top_risks: US–Iran war escalation and Strait of Hormuz disruption keeping oil above $100
Hot September CPI or NFP locking in an October Fed hike and pressuring equities
OPEC+ surprise output increase hitting crude and energy equities
Boeing SPEEA strike disrupting aerospace production
China growth undershooting stimulus despite PBOC easing
top_opportunities: US–China tariff-relief list implementation reducing trade-cliff risk
Micron's record results confirming the AI memory supercycle
China mini-stimulus supporting property and industrial demand
Big-bank Q3 earnings showing resilient credit and capital-markets activity
Potential Iran ceasefire reviving risk appetite and easing energy costs
summary: Markets are dominated by the US–Iran war and oil above $100, with ceasefire talks stalled after Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal. The Fed's September hike to 3.75–4.00% and ~73% odds of another move on Oct 27–28 make the upcoming NFP (Oct 2) and CPI (Oct 13–14) pivotal. US–China trade tensions eased via a truce extension and a $60bn tariff-relief list, while China's mini-stimulus aims to secure its GDP target. Q3 earnings season kicks off with PepsiCo, big banks, UnitedHealth and ASML, and Micron's record results validated the AI memory trade. Key idiosyncratic risks include a Boeing SPEEA strike and OPEC+ output policy.
